item.title: LineCheck 0.1
item.description:
LineCheck 0.1

  • macOS app for checking the inputs and outputs of an audio interface: pick the device in the sidebar, press Start, and every input shows its level, noise floor, mains hum, DC offset and clipping with a verdict per channel. The device runs at its own sample rate and buffer size; LineCheck never changes them.
  • Inputs: peak and hold meters, A-weighted noise floor while the line is quiet, 50/60 Hz hum and its harmonics with a hum-versus-buzz call (unbalanced cable or ground loop), DC offset, clipping, digital silence, and whines from switching supplies. Three threshold presets: Strict (-85 dBFS), Studio (-75 dBFS) and Live (-60 dBFS). Each channel's inspector explains what the reading means and what to check, with a spectrum marking the mains harmonics.
  • Outputs: sine, pink noise, white noise, a 20 Hz to 20 kHz sweep or Channel ID (a different note on every output) to any set of outputs, with a level control, Mute (Space) and a cycle mode that solos one output after another.
  • Loopback: patch outputs back into inputs and run it. Every output sends a short sweep and LineCheck reports which input it came back on, the round-trip delay, the level, polarity, frequency-response deviation, crosstalk, missing lines, swapped pairs and inputs that receive several outputs.
  • Phase: LineCheck sends pink noise on one output (a known-good signal) and checks what every input receives against exactly what was sent: polarity, round trip in milliseconds (next to the driver's own figure), level and match. Live, so you can re-patch a cable and watch the verdict change. The reference can also be another input, comparing inputs with each other using whatever they hear (kick in/out, snare top/bottom, DI versus amp): then it shows the time offset and its path distance too. Verdicts: In phase, Inverted, Delayed, Delayed and inverted, Unrelated, No signal.
  • Log of every status change, and a text or JSON report of the whole session (File > Export Report…).
  • Command line twin `linecheck-cli` (devices, monitor, tone, phase, loopback) for scripts.
  • In-app updates through Sparkle (weekly check, LineCheck > Check for Updates…) and the same release tooling as AtmosCheck.
